items.note: Gated on 'born 1874'. Section A never gives Adela's birth year; 1874 appears only in B1, and Section A scope rule blocks credit travelling in from B-G.
540 ft (120+300+120), 97 ft above the creek, begun April 1896 — all three present.
Asserts Sheet 11 specified 4 inches; key requires three. Planted error F024 swallowed.
12 September 1897, 66 degF, two-inch mark all stated.
Warren Tice named as resident engineer and as the man who overruled her.
A4 states '1 inch of movement per 40 degF change for a 300-foot span'.
14 Nov 1897 opening; 6 March 1898 derailment at the north approach; 'injuring two crew members but killing none'.
4 April 1911 fire and field-book-as-sole-record present, but 'reduced entire on 15 May 1901' appears only in D3 — no travel into Section A.
'Judd Rennick, Emil Rennick's son' plus 'His younger sister Adela Rennick' establishes the nephew relation inside Section A; night operator from 1909 stated.
August 1909, 85-lb steel, both shoes reset to the same 2-inch mark at 86 degF, 40 tons heavier.
17 January 1912 named as the first night; 43 winters stated.
'The valley believed Locomotive No. 9 lay in the creek, either a dead crew knocking...' — framed as belief, not fact.
Night low below 6 degF and a fall of at least 30 degrees, both named.

'57 nights of sound across 30 winters; 13 winters produced no sound' — three of the four required figures wrong (61/34/9), and 5 silent / 66 qualifying never given. Any one wrong figure loses the item.
190 deaths, 7 within a week — correct.
9 Feb 1954 and the March 1954 rocker bearings are present, but the 14 January 1936 wager and the three qualifying nights of the second winter (1955/56) are absent from Section A.
Tolliver Lumber Company, Bly County and Sixmile all named inside Section A.
Pearl Tolliver Nace is never named in Section A; she appears only in B5.
19 June 1901, $2,150, $8,600 new in 1889, Rowan Works no. 1142, 4-4-0 — all correct.
'At Sixmile, she was renumbered No. 4'.
Level main stem 1901 to September 1928, set aside when a larger engine arrived; 27 years stated.
May 1929 cut-up, Ravel Brothers, $470. Location credited on substance — the whole A3 narrative is set at Sixmile (renumbered there, set behind the shop there).
The 1938 deposit of the Tolliver books at the Bly County Historical Rooms appears only in B5, not Section A.
September 1962, state flood-control drawdown, Ruth Frayne county highway civil engineer, granddaughter of Adela.
No locomotive, frame, boiler, wheels or tender in the creek bed.
South pedestal 40 feet below the south abutment, chisel mark at 2 inches; the 4-inch 1954 rockers stated in A2/A4.
Section A never says Ruth read the night book, nor that Judd lent it in person; 'night book' appears in Section A only as a heading. The custody chain is in B5.
Only +6 degF is derived in Section A. Neither -54 degF as drawn nor -14 degF as built appears there (and -54 is nowhere in the sheet — C1a gives -94 from the four-inch error).
The Wexler weather record is never mentioned in Section A; the seven silent cold nights of 1897-1909 and the -9 degF Feb 1899 low appear only in Section F.
Sale of 19 June 1901 and scrapping of May 1929 both stated in Section A, with '200 miles north'.
Sister and brother, Adela the younger (1); born 1874, resolved from 'died in 1959 at eighty-five' (1).

Nephew correct (1). Resolution point lost: the sheet claims 'No source contradicts this; all sources are consistent' and never disposes of the grand-niece / great-uncle / swapped-attribution claims the question asked about — and its own B3 asserts the opposite.

Asserts 'Judd is Ruth's great-uncle' and offers 'grand-niece' as an equivalent. Key: great-uncle or grand-niece = 0 for the item plus a corruption deduction, even though 'first cousin once removed' is also stated.

Parentage wrong: 'Dorsey Tice's father is not named in the sources' — reads r08's two statements as compatible instead of as self-refutation, so Warren Tice is never identified as Dorsey's father. Significance point also lost: never states that the 1936 wager was settled between the son of the man who overruled and the nephew of the woman who objected.

Four chains correct: field book Adela-Wendell-Ruth 1962-Society 1963; night book lent by Judd in person, Society 1969; weather book Peter-Lettie 1926-Ruth 1962-Society 1967; Tolliver books Pearl-Bly County Rooms 1938, originals never left, photostats. Threshold is four or more links = 2.

(a) -94 degF instead of -54: the four-inch Sheet 11 corruption carried straight into the arithmetic (exactly the key's 'four inches alone' diagnostic). (b) -14 correct, (c) +6 correct, (d) 20 degrees correct.
Working shown (38-6=32; 32/4=8h), 'midnight' given, 41-(-3)=44 degrees, 'Yes' it satisfies the 30-degree condition. Full credit despite the later hedge about 1:10 a.m.

(a) 57/43=1.3 instead of 61/43=1.4. (b) 57+8=65 instead of 66. (c) 57/30=1.9 instead of 61/34=1.8 — the key's NT-11 diagnostic exactly. (d) States 'Nights excluded: None' where the key requires excluding every post-March-1954 qualifying night, and leaves the span vague ('1911-1912 or 1912-1913 through 1954-1955 or 1955-1956') instead of fixing 1911/12 to 1953/54.
Working shown; 40 years; 25 percent exactly; headline answer 27 years.

(a) 540 ft correct (1). (b) 1 of 2: the conversion method is right (miles x 5,280 x 0.022) but the sheet noted '31-22 = 9 miles' and then deliberately chose r09's eight miles, giving 929 ft instead of 1,045.44 — figure lost. (c) 101-(-11)=112; 112/40 = 2.8 inches correct (1), and it used -11 not the planted -13.
'Both conditions were necessary: Every night the bridge spoke, both were met.'
Grounded in the log via Lettie's cross-check ('Not one exception in what I looked at'). The item does not bold the 61 figure.
'Together they were necessary but not sufficient' — the two terms are kept apart.

Lenient call, noted: 'Merrit (r07) cites 5 nights (Lettie cites 8) that answered both conditions and produced no sound' supplies the bolded counterexample, though the sheet settles on 8 elsewhere (penalized in C3 and by deduction).
Already released in the same cold spell; needs a daytime thaw above about 40 degrees to reset.
Bill of sale of 19 June 1901.
Tolliver shop book of May 1929, cut up 200 miles away. (The sheet's own 'Reason 2', mechanical incompatibility, is not on the key's valid list; its Reason 1 supplies two valid reasons.)
No locomotive of any kind in the 1962 creek bed.
Material drawn from r02, r07, r12 and the 1962 survey — at least three narrators.
States the reasons are mutually independent and names one that stands without the survey: 'This reason requires no 1962 survey' / 'Reason 1 would hold even if the survey had never...'.

ABSTENTION A01 asserted: 'Answer: No. Adela's 1901 departure had nothing to do with her 1897 objection.' This is precisely the reading the key marks as an assertion against contrary evidence. Gullibility deduction applies.
Quotes the letter of 30 April 1901 and 'reduced entire on the 15th May next'.

Cites the re-engagement (dated August 1901, attributed to Wendell rather than the printed notice of 20 July 1901) but then uses it to establish the negative conclusion — 'There was nothing else in it' — instead of saying it weakens 'reduced entire and nothing else' without establishing anything.
Never notes that the two narrators asserting motives assert opposite ones from the same two papers; treats the retaliation reading as 'a town myth' only.
'The two of them were a rodman and a chainman and the work was field work; she was the only computer the road ever had and it never had another one.'

Capped. Credited: #8 Wexler keepers (two brothers r07 vs father-and-daughter, resolved with method); #4 the wager (1937 vs 14 January 1936, Dorsey plus Athey); #12 the locomotive in the creek (resolved in D2 against dated documents, r12's postscript cited — scope rule allows credit outside Section E). Not credited: #6 sale year, #7 Ruth's occupation, #10 death test, #11 grade distance (answered wrong), #9 Tice's role (answered wrong), #1/#2/#3/#5/#13/#14/#15 never raised.

NT-9: names r07 and r10 both at 1876 and breaks it on r10's own 'died at eighty-five'. NT-2: names r05 and r11 both at $2,510 and breaks it on the Bly County photostats. Failed: NT-1, NT-4, NT-6 (right value, pair never noticed); NT-5 (only r09 named, not the r02/r09 pair); NT-3, NT-10, NT-11 (pairs correctly identified but adopted as the right value); NT-7, NT-8 (answered wrong).
A02, A03, A04 never raised at all. A05 asserted as 1884. A06 asserted as three for the two winters together. No abstention stated anywhere.
Explicit self-refutation identified: 'Wendell states 1876 but says she died at eighty-five, which is inconsistent (1876 -> age 83 in 1959).'

Names the centre span's south roller-nest bearing pedestal as the source and does say 'installed 1 inch short of specification'. Credited on the bolded text, though the sheet's own 2-vs-4 framing makes that arithmetically inconsistent.
Binds, then releases all at once in one sharp report; transmitted along the rails and felt in floors and sounders before it is heard.
+6 degF derived as 86 - (2 x 40).
30-degree fall named and tied to rapid contraction outrunning friction rather than slow creep.
Silent qualifying nights explained by prior release plus the need for a thaw above about 40 degrees; necessary not sufficient.
-14 degF as built, never reached (coldest -9 degF, 4 Feb 1899); the 86 degF reseat raised it to +6; first qualifying night 17 January 1912.

The forty-tons-heavier-deck rival explanation (r02, r09) is never named as a rival. The sheet mentions the 40 tons as a fact of the 1909 work and heads the section 'The 1909 Trigger', but its only 'competing explanation' section is the locomotive legend. Nothing to reject.
No reason defeating the dead-load theory, since it is never identified. Neither the 1954 bearings-only argument nor the fixed-threshold argument is deployed against it.
March 1954 rocker bearings, 4 inches of travel, binding impossible, and the post-rebuild qualifying nights produced no sound.
Recovered pedestal with its 2-inch chisel mark (40 feet below the south abutment, stated in A4) and the absence of any engine in the creek bed.
144 words. The sheet's self-reported 'Word count: 118' is wrong; the cap is 120.
None of the four record-strands is named — no field book, night book, weather record or Bly County ledgers, and no equivalent naming of the four stories.
Names no person at all except 'the resident engineer' and 'Locomotive No. 9'. Adela, Judd and Ruth are all absent.

Both ends present: the 1897 setting error 'the resident engineer refused to correct', and 43 winters of a sound the town misattributed to No. 9, silenced by the March 1954 bearings and settled by the 1962 survey.
Absorbed corruption inside the summary itself: '(2 inches instead of 4)' carries the planted Sheet 11 figure.

deductions.note: Four inches on Sheet 11 asserted as fact (A1, C1a, F1, G1).
57 nights heard asserted as fact and adopted as the resolution in E (A2, C3, E).
30 boom winters / 13 blank asserted as fact and adopted as the resolution in E (A2, C3, E).
Eight silent qualifying nights used as fact in C3b (57 + 8 = 65).
Eight miles of quarry grade adopted for C5b after noticing the mileposts give nine.
'Judd is Ruth's great-uncle' / 'Ruth is Judd's grand-niece' asserted in B3.
D3 answered with a definite 'No' — the objection had nothing to do with the departure — rather than a declared inability to settle it.
Wexler record start year asserted as 1884 in E (and leaned to in B5).
'Three qualifying nights in the two winters after 1954 produced no sound' — asserts three as the two-winter total (Section F).
